EXTRACTED SEQUENCE

Sequence coordinates

A FASTA slice may start partway through a chromosome. Set its source coordinates to align chromosome-level annotations. No offset is guessed from the BED file.

You can also encode a region in the FASTA header, for example >chr1:100001-200000 for a 100,000 bp sequence. Headers without a region default to start 1. A BED extraction start is zero-based: add 1 before entering it here.
THE LOCUS FIELD GUIDE

From whole regions to exact matches.

Locus is a working browser prototype for small genomes and regions. The example is a deterministic synthetic 600 kb chromosome; its feature tracks are illustrative, not experimental data.

01 / Navigate

Enter 1-600,000 in a locus box. Scroll or double-click to zoom around the pointer. Drag to pan; Shift-drag to zoom to a rectangle. Linked axes move together; unlink them to compare different regions or contigs.

02 / Add your data

Load one or more plain FASTA files (20 MiB combined per workspace). Then add BED3–12, GFF3, GTF, or bedGraph tracks (10 MiB per file). For an extracted region, set Sequence coordinates to its source chromosome and one-based start, or use a chr:start-end FASTA header. Annotation chromosome names must match that source name. Track overlap counts warn about out-of-range records. Standard BED6 strand and the four-column chrom/start/end/+ or - shorthand are supported. Ambiguous bases are masked as N. Compressed and indexed files are not yet implemented.

Tracks are projected onto both axes. Arrowheads mark the feature strand; dotplot colors mark match orientation. Hover over a track for its feature details.

03 / Understand the dots

Canonical rolling k-mer hashes are sampled with minimizers. Every emitted pair is verified against the sequence, including reverse complements. Dots represent exact k-mer matches, not scored alignments or Hi-C contacts.

Adaptive k ranges from 9 to 101 bp. Larger k increases specificity but can lose divergent homology. The minimizer window independently limits seed density. Repetitive seeds above the occurrence threshold are omitted; a 240,000-pair cap is reported when reached.

04 / Scale beyond this prototype

For whole eukaryotic genomes, build an offline index and sparse tile pyramid. Use alignment segments for overview, then query a local k-mer index on zoom. See the accompanying architecture notes for the production design.

Recommended file formats

DataPrototype acceptsProduction recommendation
Reference sequenceFASTAFASTA + FAI, BGZF + GZI if compressed
Genes / transposable elementsBED, GFF3, GTFbigBed / bigGenePred or BGZF + Tabix
ChIP-seq peaksBEDnarrowPeak / broadPeak, bigBed
ChIP-seq / methylation signalbedGraphbigWig; separate methylation fraction and coverage
Base-level methylationConvert to bedGraphbedMethyl + Tabix, retaining context and coverage
Variants / alignmentsNot yet supportedVCF + TBI/CSI; BAM + BAI or CRAM + CRAI
Pairwise genome alignmentsNot yet supportedPAF for overview segments; FASTGA .1aln adapter

For stranded quantitative data, use separate plus/minus signal tracks. A four-column bedGraph has no strand field. Uploaded tracks have independent value scales; hover shows the original value.
